claim: Human liver cancer is dependent on extracellular glutamine.
source: Here we found that human liver cancer was dependent on extracellular glutamine.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: CB-839 as monotherapy has a very limited anticancer effect against glutamine addicted human liver cancer cells.
source: However, targeting glutamine addiction using the glutaminase inhibitor CB-839 as monotherapy had a very limited anticancer effect, even against the most glutamine addicted human liver cancer cells.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 2.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 depletes glutathione in glutamine dependent cells.
source: Mechanically, a combination of CB-839 and V-9302 depleted glutathione and induced reactive oxygen species (ROS), resulting in apoptosis of GD cells.
evidence: This mechanism is stated in the abstract and supported by metabolomics data in Figure 5.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 induces reactive oxygen species (ROS) in glutamine dependent cells.
source: Mechanically, a combination of CB-839 and V-9302 depleted glutathione and induced reactive oxygen species (ROS), resulting in apoptosis of GD cells.
evidence: This mechanism is stated in the abstract and supported by ROS measurement data in Figure 5.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 results in apoptosis of glutamine dependent cells.
source: Mechanically, a combination of CB-839 and V-9302 depleted glutathione and induced reactive oxygen species (ROS), resulting in apoptosis of GD cells.
evidence: This outcome is stated in the abstract and supported by apoptosis assay data in Figure 5.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 shows tumor inhibition in HCC xenograft mouse models in vivo.
source: Moreover, this combination also showed tumor inhibition in HCC xenograft mouse models in vivo.
evidence: This finding is stated in the abstract and supported by xenograft data in Figure 6.

claim: Liver cancer is the fourth leading cause of cancer death.
source: Liver cancer is one of the most common malignant tumors worldwide and ranks as the fourth leading cause of cancer death (Bray et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is stated in the introduction with a citation to Bray et al., 2018.

claim: Most liver cancer patients are diagnosed at an advanced stage.
source: Due to the rapid progress and delayed diagnosis, most liver cancer patients are diagnosed at an advanced stage, which leaves very few treatment options and poor prognosis.
evidence: This statement is made in the introduction based on general clinical knowledge.

claim: Sorafenib and lenvatinib provide only modest survival benefits to HCC patients with low response rates.
source: Currently approved agents, such as sorafenib and lenvatinib, provide only modest survival benefits to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients with low response rates (Llovet et al., 2008; Kudo et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is stated in the introduction with citations to Llovet et al., 2008 and Kudo et al., 2018.

claim: Nine out of eleven liver cancer cell lines are glutamine dependent.
source: Both long-term colony formation assay (Figure 1a) and short-term IncuCyte assay (Figure 1b) showed that Gln deprivation impaired the proliferation of most liver cancer cell lines (9 out of 11) in vitro.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1a and 1b.

claim: Glutamine metabolism-related genes are upregulated in liver cancer tissues compared to non-cancerous liver tissues.
source: The heatmap shows the obvious upregulation of these genes in liver cancer tissues as compared to their corresponding non-cancerous liver tissues in TCGA cohort containing 50 paired HCC samples (Figure 1c).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by the heatmap in Figure 1c.

claim: Dysregulation of glutamine metabolism genes correlates with poor prognosis of human liver cancer patients.
source: Moreover, SurvExpress survival analysis of 381 TCGA samples indicated that the dysregulation of Gln metabolism genes correlated with poor prognosis of human liver cancer patients (Figure 1f).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by survival analysis shown in Figure 1f.

claim: GLS1 mRNA levels are significantly increased in HCC tissues compared to non-tumor tissues.
source: The results indicate that mRNA levels of GLS1 are significantly increased in HCC tissues compared to non-tumor tissues (Figure 2a).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2a.

claim: GLS1 level is increased to more than double in about 55% of HCC patients.
source: Among the 229 paired samples, the GLS1 level is increased to more than double in about 55% of HCC patients (Figure 2b).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2b.

claim: High mRNA level of GLS1 correlates with poor prognosis of human liver cancer patients.
source: TCGA data indicated that the high mRNA level of GLS1 correlated with the poor prognosis of human liver cancer patients (Figure 2c).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by survival analysis in Figure 2c.

claim: HCC patients with high protein expression of GLS1 exhibit worse overall survival compared to patients with low protein expression of GLS1.
source: The Kaplan-Meier analysis indicates that HCC patients with high protein expression of GLS1 exhibit worse overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) as compared to patients with low protein expression of GLS1 (Figure 2d,e and f).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Kaplan-Meier analysis in Figure 2d, e, and f.

claim: HCC patients with high protein expression of GLS1 exhibit worse disease-free survival compared to patients with low protein expression of GLS1.
source: The Kaplan-Meier analysis indicates that HCC patients with high protein expression of GLS1 exhibit worse overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) as compared to patients with low protein expression of GLS1 (Figure 2d,e and f).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Kaplan-Meier analysis in Figure 2d, e, and f.

claim: CB-839 treatment severely impairs the proliferation of only three glutamine dependent cell lines.
source: We found that CB-839 treatment only severely impaired the proliferation of three GD cell lines (Figure 2g and h).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2g and h.

claim: There is no correlation between protein level of GLS1 and CB-839 sensitivity.
source: We also analyzed the correlation between CB-839 sensitivity and expression level of its target and found no correlation between protein level of GLS1 and CB-839 sensitivity (Figure 2g, h and i).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2g, h, and i.

claim: The protein level of GLS1 is not correlated to glutamine addiction in vitro.
source: In addition, the protein level of GLS1 was not correlated to Gln addiction in vitro (Figures 1a, b and 2i), indicating that Gln addiction to liver cancer cells is not dependent on GLS1 level.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data in Figures 1a, b, and 2i.

claim: Glutamine addiction to liver cancer cells is not dependent on GLS1 level.
source: In addition, the protein level of GLS1 was not correlated to Gln addiction in vitro (Figures 1a, b and 2i), indicating that Gln addiction to liver cancer cells is not dependent on GLS1 level.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the text and inferred from the lack of correlation shown in Figures 1a, b, and 2i.

claim: CB-839 treatment significantly decreases glutamate levels in SNU398 and HepG2 cells.
source: We found that CB-839 treatment significantly decreased a number of key downstream metabolites involved in Gln metabolism, such as glutamate (GLU), TCA cycle intermediate (α-KG), redox metabolite (glutathione, NADPH) in both cell lines (Figure 3a and b and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by metabolomics data in Figure 3a and b.

claim: CB-839 treatment significantly decreases α-KG levels in SNU398 and HepG2 cells.
source: We found that CB-839 treatment significantly decreased a number of key downstream metabolites involved in Gln metabolism, such as glutamate (GLU), TCA cycle intermediate (α-KG), redox metabolite (glutathione, NADPH) in both cell lines (Figure 3a and b and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by metabolomics data in Figure 3a and b.

claim: CB-839 treatment significantly decreases glutathione levels in SNU398 and HepG2 cells.
source: We found that CB-839 treatment significantly decreased a number of key downstream metabolites involved in Gln metabolism, such as glutamate (GLU), TCA cycle intermediate (α-KG), redox metabolite (glutathione, NADPH) in both cell lines (Figure 3a and b and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by metabolomics data in Figure 3a and b.

claim: CB-839 treatment significantly decreases NADPH levels in SNU398 and HepG2 cells.
source: We found that CB-839 treatment significantly decreased a number of key downstream metabolites involved in Gln metabolism, such as glutamate (GLU), TCA cycle intermediate (α-KG), redox metabolite (glutathione, NADPH) in both cell lines (Figure 3a and b and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by metabolomics data in Figure 3a and b.

claim: CB-839 efficiently blocks glutamine utilization and interferes with the dynamic changes of intermediates in glutamine metabolism.
source: These results indicate that CB-839 efficiently blocks Gln utilization and interferes with the dynamic changes of intermediates in Gln metabolism.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the text and inferred from the metabolomics data showing decreased metabolite levels.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 shows synergistic anti-proliferation effect in glutamine dependent cell lines.
source: Indeed, the combination showed synergistic anti-proliferation effect in GD cell lines, but only showed limited anti-tumor effect in GID cell lines in vitro (Figure 4a,b and c and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 4a, b, c, and supplement 1.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 shows limited anti-tumor effect in glutamine independent cell lines.
source: Indeed, the combination showed synergistic anti-proliferation effect in GD cell lines, but only showed limited anti-tumor effect in GID cell lines in vitro (Figure 4a,b and c and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 4a, b, c, and supplement 1.

claim: CB-839 or V-9302 alone significantly decreases the level of GSH in SNU398 and HepG2 cells.
source: The results show that CB-839 or V-9302 alone significantly decreased the level of GSH, while the combination resulted in a further decrease in GSH in both cell lines (Figure 5a).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by GSH measurement data in Figure 5a.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 results in a further decrease in GSH compared to single agents in SNU398 and HepG2 cells.
source: The results show that CB-839 or V-9302 alone significantly decreased the level of GSH, while the combination resulted in a further decrease in GSH in both cell lines (Figure 5a).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by GSH measurement data in Figure 5a.

claim: Single agent CB-839 or V-9302 only modestly increases ROS production.
source: Analysis of intracellular ROS levels showed that single agent CB-839 or V-9302 only modestly increased the ROS production.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by ROS measurement data in Figure 5b.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 dramatically increases ROS production.
source: However, their combination dramatically increased the already-elevated ROS production, reaching a level that caused severe DNA damage, as evidenced by an increase in γ-H2AX (Figure 5b and c).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by ROS measurement data in Figure 5b and western blot in Figure 5c.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 causes severe DNA damage as evidenced by an increase in γ-H2AX.
source: However, their combination dramatically increased the already-elevated ROS production, reaching a level that caused severe DNA damage, as evidenced by an increase in γ-H2AX (Figure 5b and c).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by western blot data in Figure 5c.

claim: NAC treatment rescues the cell viability and proliferation of SNU398 and HepG2 cells in the presence of both CB-839 and V-9302.
source: The results show that NAC treatment rescued the cell viability and proliferation of SNU398 and HepG2 cells in the presence of both CB-839 and V-9302 (Figure 5d and e).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 5d and e.

claim: The synergistic induction of apoptosis by CB-839 and V-9302 can be rescued by NAC treatment in SNU398 and HepG2 cells.
source: Moreover, the strong synergistic induction of apoptosis can be rescued by NAC treatment in both SNU398 and HepG2 cells, as indicated by the IncuCyte caspase-3/7 apoptosis assay (Figure 5f).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by apoptosis assay data in Figure 5f.

claim: GLS1 inhibition by CB-839 reduces mitochondrial glutamate level.
source: GLS1 inhibition by CB-839 reduces mitochondrial Glu level, which decreases TCA-dependent NADPH production, elevating glutathione oxidation.
evidence: This mechanism is stated in the text as part of the model explaining synergy.

claim: GLS1 inhibition by CB-839 decreases TCA-dependent NADPH production.
source: GLS1 inhibition by CB-839 reduces mitochondrial Glu level, which decreases TCA-dependent NADPH production, elevating glutathione oxidation.
evidence: This mechanism is stated in the text as part of the model explaining synergy.

claim: GLS1 inhibition by CB-839 elevates glutathione oxidation.
source: GLS1 inhibition by CB-839 reduces mitochondrial Glu level, which decreases TCA-dependent NADPH production, elevating glutathione oxidation.
evidence: This mechanism is stated in the text as part of the model explaining synergy.

claim: CB-839 decreases intracellular glutamate that is essential for cystine import by xCT.
source: Besides, CB-839 also decreases intracellular Glu that is essential for cystine import by xCT, a cystine/glutamate antiporter, thus cutting down the cysteine conversion that in turn serves as the rate-limiting precursor for GSH biosynthesis.
evidence: This mechanism is stated in the text as part of the model explaining synergy.

claim: Cysteine serves as the rate-limiting precursor for GSH biosynthesis.
source: Besides, CB-839 also decreases intracellular Glu that is essential for cystine import by xCT, a cystine/glutamate antiporter, thus cutting down the cysteine conversion that in turn serves as the rate-limiting precursor for GSH biosynthesis.
evidence: This is stated in the text and represents established biochemical knowledge.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 elicits strong growth inhibition in SNU398 xenograft models.
source: Results showed that the combination elicited a strong growth inhibition in both SNU398 and MHCC97H xenograft models, while single-drug treatment showed modest anti-tumor effects (Figure 6a,b,c and d).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by xenograft data in Figure 6a and b.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 elicits strong growth inhibition in MHCC97H xenograft models.
source: Results showed that the combination elicited a strong growth inhibition in both SNU398 and MHCC97H xenograft models, while single-drug treatment showed modest anti-tumor effects (Figure 6a,b,c and d).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by xenograft data in Figure 6c and d.

claim: Single-drug treatment with CB-839 or V-9302 shows modest anti-tumor effects in xenograft models.
source: Results showed that the combination elicited a strong growth inhibition in both SNU398 and MHCC97H xenograft models, while single-drug treatment showed modest anti-tumor effects (Figure 6a,b,c and d).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by xenograft data in Figure 6.

claim: No body weight reduction was observed in all treatment groups in xenograft studies.
source: We also measured the body weight of mice during the treatment, and no body weight reduction was observed in all the treatment groups (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), indicating good tolerability for this novel drug combination.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by body weight data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 has good tolerability in xenograft models.
source: We also measured the body weight of mice during the treatment, and no body weight reduction was observed in all the treatment groups (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), indicating good tolerability for this novel drug combination.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the text and inferred from the lack of body weight reduction.

claim: Treatment with the combination of CB-839 and V-9302 results in an obvious decrease in Ki67 positive cells in xenograft tumors.
source: IHC analyses showed that treatment with the combination of CB-839 and V-9302 resulted in an obvious decrease in Ki67 positive cells (Figure 6e,f,g and j).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by IHC data in Figure 6e, f, g, and j.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 significantly increases caspase-3 positive cells in xenograft tumors.
source: In addition, the combination also significantly increased caspase-3 positive cells (Figure 6e,f,h and k) and γH2AX-positive cells (Figure 6e,f,i and l) in tumor tissues, supporting the induction of apoptosis and DNA damage in vivo.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by IHC data in Figure 6e, f, h, and k.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 significantly increases γH2AX-positive cells in xenograft tumors.
source: In addition, the combination also significantly increased caspase-3 positive cells (Figure 6e,f,h and k) and γH2AX-positive cells (Figure 6e,f,i and l) in tumor tissues, supporting the induction of apoptosis and DNA damage in vivo.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by IHC data in Figure 6e, f, i, and l.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 induces apoptosis in vivo.
source: In addition, the combination also significantly increased caspase-3 positive cells (Figure 6e,f,h and k) and γH2AX-positive cells (Figure 6e,f,i and l) in tumor tissues, supporting the induction of apoptosis and DNA damage in vivo.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the text and supported by IHC data showing increased caspase-3 positive cells.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 induces DNA damage in vivo.
source: In addition, the combination also significantly increased caspase-3 positive cells (Figure 6e,f,h and k) and γH2AX-positive cells (Figure 6e,f,i and l) in tumor tissues, supporting the induction of apoptosis and DNA damage in vivo.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the text and supported by IHC data showing increased γH2AX-positive cells.

claim: CB-839 is a potent and noncompetitive allosteric GLS1 inhibitor.
source: CB-839 (also known as telaglenastat) is a potent and noncompetitive allosteric GLS1 inhibitor.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about CB-839.

claim: CB-839 exhibits significant anti-proliferative activity in several types of cancer cell lines and xenografts.
source: It exhibits significant anti-proliferative activity in several types of cancer cell lines and xenografts such as triple-negative breast cancer (Gross et al., 2014), lung adenocarcinoma (Galan-Cobo et al., 2019), chondrosarcoma (Peterse et al., 2018), and lymphoma cancer (Xiang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is stated in the introduction with multiple citations.

claim: CB-839 overcomes metabolic adaptation to the mTOR inhibitor MLN128 in xenografts and patient-derived xenografts of lung squamous cell carcinomas.
source: CB-839 overcomes metabolic adaptation to the mTOR inhibitor MLN128 in xenografts and patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) of lung squamous cell carcinomas (Momcilovic et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is stated in the introduction with a citation to Momcilovic et al., 2018.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and CDK4/6 inhibitors has shown promising results in human esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
source: Moreover, the combination of CB-839 and CDK4/6 inhibitors has shown promising results in human esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (Qie et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is stated in the introduction with a citation to Qie et al., 2019.

claim: CB-839 is under evaluation for the treatment of hematological malignancies and solid tumors in several phase I-II clinical trials.
source: CB-839 is also under evaluation for the treatment of hematological malignancies and solid tumors in several phase I-II clinical trials (Song et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is stated in the introduction with a citation to Song et al., 2018.

claim: Glutaminolysis converts glutamine to glutamate, which is catalyzed by mitochondrial glutaminase (GLS).
source: Glutaminolysis converts glutamine to glutamate, which is catalyzed by mitochondrial glutaminase (GLS), and then further converted into tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle metabolites, generating ATP and NADPH.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established biochemical knowledge.

claim: Glutaminolysis is directly involved in the regulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis.
source: Glutaminolysis is also directly involved in the regulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis by providing not only precursors glutamate and cysteine for glutathione (GSH) synthesis but also promoting the production of NADPH via glutamate dehydrogenase (GLUD; Altman et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is stated in the introduction with a citation to Altman et al., 2016.

claim: Many tumor types are particularly dependent on glutamine for proliferation and survival.
source: Many tumor types, such as pancreatic cancer (Son et al., 2013), acute myeloid leukemia (AML; Jacque et al., 2015), breast cancer (Gross et al., 2014), and lung cancer (Wang et al., 2018), are particularly dependent on glutamine for proliferation and survival, as glutamine controls oxidative phosphorylation, nucleotide biosynthesis, and redox homeostasis in these cells, and removal of glutamine leads to apoptosis.
evidence: This claim is stated in the introduction with multiple citations.

claim: GLS1 regulates the stemness properties of HCC.
source: Recently, it is reported that GLS1, one major isoform of GLS, regulates the stemness properties of HCC, and targeting GLS1 achieved some therapeutic effect against HCC cells (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is stated in the introduction with a citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: Targeting GLS1 achieved some therapeutic effect against HCC cells.
source: Recently, it is reported that GLS1, one major isoform of GLS, regulates the stemness properties of HCC, and targeting GLS1 achieved some therapeutic effect against HCC cells (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is stated in the introduction with a citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: ASCT2 is a sodium-dependent solute carrier protein responsible for the import of neutral amino acids.
source: The alanine-serine-cysteine transporter, type-2 (ASCT2, encoded by gene SLC1A5), is a sodium-dependent solute carrier protein responsible for the import of neutral amino acids and is the primary transporter of glutamine in cancer cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as established knowledge about ASCT2.

claim: ASCT2 is the primary transporter of glutamine in cancer cells.
source: The alanine-serine-cysteine transporter, type-2 (ASCT2, encoded by gene SLC1A5), is a sodium-dependent solute carrier protein responsible for the import of neutral amino acids and is the primary transporter of glutamine in cancer cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as established knowledge about ASCT2.

claim: Several studies have attributed glutathione synthesis and ROS stress with dysregulation of ASCT2.
source: Several studies have attributed glutathione (GSH) synthesis and ROS stress with dysregulation of ASCT2 (Schulte et al., 2018; Yoo et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is stated in the results section with citations to Schulte et al., 2018 and Yoo et al., 2020.

claim: GSH is an important antioxidant that acts as a free radical scavenger upon its reaction with ROS in cells.
source: GSH is an important antioxidant that acts as a free radical scavenger upon its reaction with ROS in cells (Bansal and Simon, 2018; Okazaki et al., 2017), raising the possibility that combination of CB-839 and V-9302 may interfere with ROS homeostasis of these liver cancer cells.
evidence: This claim is stated in the results section with citations to Bansal and Simon, 2018 and Okazaki et al., 2017.

claim: De novo pyrimidine synthesis was identified as a metabolic vulnerability of triple-negative breast cancer.
source: For example, de novo pyrimidine synthesis was identified as a metabolic vulnerability of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), suggesting that inhibition of pyrimidine synthesis could sensitize TNBC to chemotherapy (Brown et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Brown et al., 2017.

claim: Cisplatin-resistant cancer cells are strongly dependent on glutamine for nucleotide biosynthesis.
source: Cisplatin-resistant cancer cells were found to be strongly dependent on glutamine for nucleotide biosynthesis and therefore became exquisitely sensitive to treatment with antimetabolites that target nucleoside metabolism (Obrist et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Obrist et al., 2018.

claim: The HGF-MET axis inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (PDHC) activity but activates GLS to facilitate glutaminolysis in multiple liver cancer cells.
source: The HGF-MET axis was reported to inhibit pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (PDHC) activity but activate GLS to facilitate glutaminolysis in multiple liver cancer cells (Huang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Huang et al., 2019.

claim: The downregulation of Sirtuin four in liver cancer promotes HCC tumorigenesis via enhancing glutamine metabolism and regulating ADP/AMP levels.
source: Another study reported that the downregulation of Sirtuin four in liver cancer promoted HCC tumorigenesis via enhancing glutamine metabolism and regulating ADP/AMP levels (Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Wang et al., 2019.

claim: MYC-induced mouse liver tumors have increased GLS expression and decreased glutamate-ammonia ligase (GLUL) expression relative to surrounding tissues.
source: In addition, MYC-induced mouse liver tumors had increased GLS expression and decreased glutamate-ammonia ligase (GLUL) expression relative to surrounding tissues, exhibiting elevated Gln catabolism (Xiang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Xiang et al., 2015.

claim: MYC-induced mouse liver tumors exhibit elevated glutamine catabolism.
source: In addition, MYC-induced mouse liver tumors had increased GLS expression and decreased glutamate-ammonia ligase (GLUL) expression relative to surrounding tissues, exhibiting elevated Gln catabolism (Xiang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Xiang et al., 2015.

claim: There is debate about the target selectivity of V-9302 for ASCT2.
source: However, there is still some debate about the target selectivity of V-9302 for ASCT2. Broer et al (Angelika et al., 2018) reported that V-9302 did not inhibit ASCT2 and glutamine uptake, but rather blocked sodium-neutral amino acid transporter 2 (SNAT2) and the large neutral amino acid transporter 1 (LAT1).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Angelika et al., 2018.

claim: V-9302 blocks sodium-neutral amino acid transporter 2 (SNAT2) and the large neutral amino acid transporter 1 (LAT1).
source: Broer et al (Angelika et al., 2018) reported that V-9302 did not inhibit ASCT2 and glutamine uptake, but rather blocked sodium-neutral amino acid transporter 2 (SNAT2) and the large neutral amino acid transporter 1 (LAT1).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Angelika et al., 2018.

claim: Both SNAT2 and LAT1 can mediate glutamine uptake in most cancer cells.
source: Interestingly, it has been reported that, in addition to ASCT2, both SNAT2 and LAT1 also can mediate glutamine uptake in most cancer cells (Bröer and Bröer, 2017).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Bröer and Bröer, 2017.

claim: CB-839 induced metabolic vulnerability can be enhanced by OXPHOS inhibitor IACS-10759, PPP inhibitor DHEA, and PHGDH inhibitor NCT503.
source: Impressively, we find that the CB-839 induced metabolic vulnerability also can be further enhanced by other several anti-metabolic drugs such as OXPHOS inhibitor IACS-10759, PPP inhibitor DHEA, and PHGDH inhibitor NCT503 (Figure 3d).
evidence: This finding is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 3d.

claim: Chronic liver disease has impaired liver function and usually leads to dysfunction of ammonia metabolism.
source: Chronic liver disease has impaired liver function and usually leads to dysfunction of ammonia metabolism.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as established clinical knowledge.

claim: There is a general correlation between higher levels of ammonia and more severe encephalopathy in cirrhosis.
source: For example, there is a general correlation between higher levels of ammonia and more severe encephalopathy in cirrhosis (Olde Damink et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Olde Damink et al., 2002.

claim: GLS plays important roles in liver ammonia metabolism.
source: As a mitochondrial enzyme, GLS plays important roles in liver ammonia metabolism (Botman et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Botman et al., 2014.

claim: There are two distinct isoforms of GLS, GLS1 and GLS2, which possess discrete tissue distribution, structural properties, and molecular regulation.
source: There are two distinct isoforms of GLS, GLS1 and GLS2, which possess discrete tissue distribution, structural properties, and molecular regulation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as established knowledge about GLS isoforms.

claim: The GLS1 gene encodes two isoforms, kidney-type glutaminase (KGA, long transcript isoform) and the glutaminase C (GAC, short transcript isoform).
source: The GLS1 gene encodes two isoforms, kidney-type glutaminase (KGA, long transcript isoform) and the glutaminase C (GAC, short transcript isoform), which are expressed in kidneys and in a variety of other tissues including cancer cells (Katt et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Katt et al., 2017.

claim: GLS2 is strongly expressed and active in periportal hepatocytes.
source: The GLS2 gene is strongly expressed and active in periportal hepatocytes, where they generate glutamate and release ammonia for urea synthesis (Katt et al., 2017; Curthoys and Watford, 1995).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with citations to Katt et al., 2017 and Curthoys and Watford, 1995.

claim: CB-839 selectively inhibits GLS1 but not GLS2.
source: Interestingly enough, CB-839 selectively inhibits GLS1 but not GLS2 (Gross et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Gross et al., 2014.

claim: GLS inhibition by CB-839 treatment is less likely to pose a problem for HCC patients with impaired ammonia metabolism.
source: Taken together, although many HCC patients co-exist liver disease and thus usually have impaired ammonia metabolism, GLS inhibition by CB-839 treatment is less likely to pose a problem for these patients.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the discussion and inferred from the selective inhibition of GLS1 by CB-839.

claim: 18F-BnTP is a voltage-sensitive, positron emission tomography (PET) radiotracer that measures mitochondrial membrane potential in non-small-cell lung cancer.
source: Recently, a voltage-sensitive, positron emission tomography (PET) radiotracer known as 18F-BnTP was developed to measure mitochondrial membrane potential in non-small-cell lung cancer.
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion as an example of metabolism-targeted imaging.

claim: Only mouse tumors with a high uptake of 18F-BnTP show marked growth suppression when treated with oxidative-phosphorylation inhibitor IACS-010759.
source: It was found that only mouse tumors with a high uptake of 18F-BnTP showed marked growth suppression when treated with oxidative-phosphorylation inhibitor IACS-010759 (Momcilovic et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Momcilovic et al., 2019.

claim: [18F]fluoro-2-deoxyglucose (18F-FDG) is widely used in clinical use for diagnosing and staging cancer.
source: Another example is the widespread use of a radioisotope labeled glucose analog, [18F]fluoro-2-deoxyglucose (18F-FDG), in clinical use for diagnosing and staging cancer (Kelloff et al., 2005; Nair et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with citations to Kelloff et al., 2005 and Nair et al., 2012.

claim: 18F-FDG undergoes cellular uptake via the same pathway as glucose but becomes trapped intracellularly after phosphorylation by hexokinase.
source: 18F-FDG undergoes cellular uptake via the same pathway as glucose but becomes trapped intracellularly after phosphorylation by hexokinase, which can be visualized by PET imaging and used to detect glucose uptake in tumors.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as established knowledge about 18F-FDG.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 only shows synergy in liver tumors that are addicted to glutamine.
source: In our study, we find that the combination of CB-839 and V-9302 only shows synergy in liver tumors that are addicted to Gln.
evidence: This finding is stated in the discussion and supported by experimental data showing differential effects in GD vs GID cells.

claim: Measuring glutamine uptake or glutamine addiction is of potential importance for selecting patients that might benefit from the combination of CB-839 and V-9302.
source: It suggests that measuring Gln uptake or Gln addiction is of potential importance for selecting patients that might benefit from this combination.
evidence: This suggestion is stated in the discussion and inferred from the selective efficacy in GD tumors.

claim: 11C-Gln was shown to visualize glutaminolytic tumors in vivo as a metabolic marker for probing glutamine-addicted tumor.
source: Tracer 11C-Gln was shown to visualize glutaminolytic tumors in vivo as a metabolic marker for probing glutamine-addicted tumor (Qu et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Qu et al., 2012.

claim: 18F-(2S,4R)4-FGln PET was reported to track cellular glutamine pool size in breast cancers with differential GLS activity.
source: Similarly, 18F-(2S,4R)4-FGln PET was reported to track cellular Gln pool size in breast cancers with differential GLS activity and applied as a response marker for CB-839 (Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Zhou et al., 2017.

claim: 18F-(2S,4R)4-FGln PET can be applied as a response marker for CB-839.
source: Similarly, 18F-(2S,4R)4-FGln PET was reported to track cellular Gln pool size in breast cancers with differential GLS activity and applied as a response marker for CB-839 (Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion with a citation to Zhou et al., 2017.

claim: Dual inhibition of glutamine metabolism by targeting both glutaminase and glutamine transporter ASCT2 represents a potential novel treatment strategy for glutamine addicted liver cancers.
source: Our findings indicate that dual inhibition of glutamine metabolism by targeting both glutaminase and glutamine transporter ASCT2 represents a potential novel treatment strategy for glutamine addicted liver cancers.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the abstract and represents the main finding of the study.

claim: The combination of CB-839 and V-9302 achieves a synergistic anti-tumor effect in liver cancer via disrupting the GSH/ROS balance.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that the combination of CB-839 and V-9302 achieves a synergistic anti-tumor effect in liver cancer via disrupting the GSH/ROS balance.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the results section and supported by GSH and ROS measurement data.

claim: CB-839 treated cells are vulnerable to other perturbations that further deplete glutamine anaplerosis, such as blockage of major glutamine transporter ASCT-2 by V-9302.
source: CB-839 treated cells are vulnerable to other perturbations that further deplete glutamine anaplerosis, such as blockage of major Gln transporter ASCT-2 by V-9302.
evidence: This mechanism is stated in the results section as part of the model explaining synergy.

claim: The combination of BPTES and V-9302 shows similar synergistic effects as CB-839 and V-9302 in liver cancer cell lines.
source: Moreover, similar results were observed in these cell lines when combining V-9302 with another GLS1 inhibitor BPTES (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: xCT is a cystine/glutamate antiporter.
source: Besides, CB-839 also decreases intracellular Glu that is essential for cystine import by xCT, a cystine/glutamate antiporter, thus cutting down the cysteine conversion that in turn serves as the rate-limiting precursor for GSH biosynthesis.
evidence: This is stated in the text as established knowledge about xCT.
